definition: The universal quantum-verified currency (symbol: Φ) — simultaneously money and a claim on quantum computational energy. Each unit is physically uncopyable, backed by the laws of physics. Every Quanta represents both exchange value and a redeemable right to processing time on the global EDN network, making everyone who holds Quanta a fractional owner of civilization's computing infrastructure.
origin: From quantum mechanics — each unit exists as a unique quantum state that cannot be duplicated. The compute equivalence was established in 2174 when Sterling-Nakamura opened the EDN idle cycles to market purchase.
example: Fifty thousand Quanta for a clean extraction. Half up front.
